title: RN 8 Salary NSW Per Hour: Convert to Annual, Fortnightly and Weekly Pay
description: Convert rn 8 salary nsw per hour to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, minimum wage and casual loading estimates.
salarySummary: Assuming a 38-hour week and 52 weeks, an hourly rate of $26.44 (National Minimum Wage) gives an annual gross of about $52,200, a fortnightly gross of about $2,009, and a weekly gross of about $1,004.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to the rn 8 salary nsw per hour rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If your rn 8 salary nsw per hour is a base rate, you would add 25% to get the casual rate. If your rate already includes casual loading, do not add it again. The National Minimum Wage casual rate from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your ordinary earnings for a 38-hour week are $1,140. The super contribution would be $136.80, added to your pay by your employer. Super stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: What tax is deducted from an hourly wage in NSW?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy of 2% also applies. The estimate here uses the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds. Your actual tax depends on your total income and circumstances.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the RN 8 Salary NSW Per Hour Conversion

If you're searching for **rn 8 salary nsw per hour**, you likely want to know what that hourly figure means in annual, fortnightly and weekly terms. This guide explains the standard conversion using a 38-hour week and a 52-week year, and covers tax, super, minimum wage and casual loading. The figures come from the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Bureau of Statistics and Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard way to estimate annual gross pay is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For example, if your **rn 8 salary nsw per hour** is $40 and you work 38 hours every week, your annual gross pay is:

$40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances or salary sacrifice. It's a starting point for budgeting and comparing offers. When no other hours are specified, we assume a 38-hour week, which is the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the same $40 per hour example:

- Weekly: $40 × 38 = $1,520
- Fortnightly: $1,520 × 2 = $3,040

Many employers in NSW pay fortnightly, so this figure is useful for planning your cash flow. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see these amounts instantly.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most workers in NSW are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. The **rn 8 salary nsw per hour** you see may be an award rate, an enterprise agreement rate, or a market rate. Always check the relevant award via the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) to confirm the correct minimum.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. The casual minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When using the [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading; enter the base rate and let the tool add the loading. If your **rn 8 salary nsw per hour** already includes the loading, treat it as the casual rate and do not add it again.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12%. Super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings (usually your base hourly rate times hours worked) and is not deducted from your pay. For example, if your weekly ordinary earnings are $1,520, your employer adds $182.40 in super. Super stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This estimate uses 12% of ordinary earnings only.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The estimate here uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This is not a tax determination; use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

### Using the NSW Full-Time Average as a Reference

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales averaged $2,108.80 per week. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job such as a registered nurse. If you are comparing your **rn 8 salary nsw per hour** to this figure, remember it is an average, not the median for your role. The national full-time average was $2,083.70 per week. Your actual rate may be higher or lower depending on your award, experience and location.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, see the [reference tables](/data) for award rates and the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. You can also explore [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to understand how salary packaging affects your take-home pay.
